Container.Name: coffee-tracker
Container.Overview: Self-hosted coffee catalog: rate coffees over time, snap a bag photo to auto-fill the form (OCR), multi-user. Serves the Angular PWA and the API same-origin on port 8080. Place behind a reverse proxy that terminates HTTPS.
Container.Requires: Set a strong Jwt__Key (e.g. `openssl rand -base64 48`); the app refuses to start without one. A fresh instance accepts exactly one account: register, and the first user becomes admin while registration closes behind them. Put the container behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy and set ForwardedHeaders__KnownProxies to the proxy's name or IP.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: HTTP port the app listens on. Map your reverse proxy to this.

Config.Name: Config (SQLite DB)
Config.Description: Holds coffee.db. Back this up before updating the image.

Config.Name: Photos
Config.Description: Uploaded coffee photos. Back this up before updating.

Config.Name: JWT Signing Key
Config.Description: REQUIRED. Long random secret for signing auth tokens. The app refuses to start without a strong value. Generate e.g. with: openssl rand -base64 48

Config.Name: OIDC Authority
Config.Description: Base URL of an OpenID Connect provider (Authelia, Keycloak, Authentik...). Set it together with OIDC Client Id to offer sign-in through that provider; leave both empty for app accounts only. Must be https (http is accepted on loopback only). Anyone the provider lets through gets an account, so use a provider that gates who may sign in.

Config.Name: OIDC Client Id
Config.Description: The client id registered with that provider, a public client using the authorization code flow with PKCE, with this app's root URL as its redirect URI. Required whenever OIDC Authority is set.

Config.Name: OIDC Display Name
Config.Description: What to call the provider on the sign-in button (e.g. Authelia). Left empty, the button reads 'your identity provider'.

Config.Name: OIDC Scopes
Config.Description: Scopes requested from the provider. Add 'groups' if you use the admin claim mapping.

Config.Name: OIDC Admin Claim
Config.Description: Claim carrying the administrator assertion (e.g. groups). Set together with OIDC Admin Claim Value; both or neither. Left empty, the first user to sign in through the provider becomes admin.

Config.Name: OIDC Admin Claim Value
Config.Description: Value the admin claim must carry to grant administrator rights. Re-evaluated on every sign-in, so removing someone from the group revokes their rights at their next sign-in.

Config.Name: Known Proxies
Config.Description: Comma-separated host names or IPs of your reverse proxy (e.g. swag). Lets the app trust X-Forwarded-* headers. Prefer a name: a pinned IP holds only until the proxy restarts onto another one. Names are resolved at startup.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID for file permissions. Set this to match your host user's UID so the container can read/write the mounted /config and /photos volumes (default: 99 for Unraid 'nobody'). NOTE: on startup the container recursively chowns /config and /photos to this owner, point them at dedicated directories, not a shared/pre-existing share. 0 (root) is refused.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID for file permissions. Set this to match your host group's GID (default: 100 for Unraid 'users').
